newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen International says it beat '96 net target.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen International says it beat '96 net target.

text.p: Retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise Co Ltd estimates it beat its 1996 net profit target of 54.32 million yuan, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

More than 60 percent of earnings last year came from the sale of its 50 percent-owned 81,000 square metre Guoqi Building, an office complex in the centre of Shenzhen which was completed at the end of 1995.
The remainder came from its retail operations, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.
Precise profit figures would not be made public until an audit was completed, he added.
The spokesman said the firm expected year-on-year growth of 10 percent in net earnings in 1997 through efforts to expand its retailing business.

The company plans to expand its retail space by 24,000 sq metres to 35,950 sq metres this year. It will open three new stores in different locations around Guangdong, including one in Shenzhen, the official said, but did not give details.
The company said net profit in the first half of 1996 rocketed 325 percent to 30.84 million yuan over 7.26 million yuan in the year-earlier period, under Chinese accounting standards.
It had after-tax profits of 40.83 million yuan in 1995 and 26.49 million yuan the previous year.
